london.name: Mildreds
london.note: London vegan institution since 1988; fully plant-based menu with clearly marked gluten-free, nut-free and soya-free options and big seasonal variety.

london.name: Gauthier Soho
london.note: Michelin-trained chef Alexis Gauthier's fully vegan French fine-dining townhouse; tasting menus built on classical technique, all plant-based.

london.name: Purezza
london.note: Fully vegan pizzeria with house-made plant cheeses and a dedicated gluten-free sourdough base praised by coeliac diners.

london.name: Itadaki Zen
london.note: Completely vegan Japanese kitchen near King's Cross serving vegan sushi, gyoza, ramen and udon from organic produce.

london.name: Manna
london.note: London's first vegetarian restaurant, now entirely plant-based; long-standing spot for creative meat-free cooking near Chalk Farm.

london.name: Vantra
london.note: Fully vegan and gluten-free Soho sanctuary doing tamari ramen, laksa, dan dan noodles and v-chicken satay in one dietary-safe menu.

london.name: Mallow
london.note: From the team behind Mildreds; refined seasonal vegan small plates and weekend brunch in Borough Market, all plant-based.

london.name: Ottolenghi Islington
london.note: Yotam Ottolenghi's flagship; counter and dinner menus with abundant vegetarian mezze, salads and desserts alongside some meat dishes.

london.name: Bubala
london.note: Entirely vegetarian Middle Eastern small plates with plenty of vegan options: burnt-butter hummus, halloumi, confit potato latkes.

london.name: Sagar
london.note: Vegetarian and vegan South Indian chain branch; dosas, thalis and idli with clear vegan labelling and gluten-free friendly items.

london.name: The Gate
london.note: Classic vegetarian restaurant in a converted church hall; eclectic global menu strong on vegan and vegetarian choice.

london.name: Niche Gluten-Free Dining
london.note: London's first 100% gluten-free (also nut- and sesame-free) restaurant; coeliac diners can order anything on the comfort-food menu.

london.name: Honest Burgers
london.note: Dedicated gluten-free fryers, GF buns for every burger, GF onion rings, plus vegan plant patties; a coeliac-safe chain favourite.

london.name: Copains
london.note: 100% gluten-free Parisian-style bakery with vegan-friendly pastries: pistachio cronuts, babka, focaccia and breads.

london.name: Reubens
london.note: Long-running kosher deli on Baker Street famed for salt beef sandwiches, kneidlach soup and latkes under kosher supervision.

london.name: La Fiesta
london.note: Glatt kosher Argentinian grill in the heart of Golders Green; kosher steaks and South American dishes evenings only.

london.name: Sami's
london.note: Kosher meat restaurant on Golders Green Road (London Beit Din) serving grills, shawarma and Middle Eastern mains.

london.name: Poppies Fish & Chips
london.note: Halal-friendly chippy: fish is fried free of alcohol in groundnut oil and can be cooked separately on request; alcohol served on site.

london.name: Tayyabs
london.note: Iconic Whitechapel Punjabi grill since 1972 with a fully halal menu; famous for lamb chops and karahi, BYOB, vegetarian options too.

london.name: Urumchi Uyghur Restaurant
london.note: Halal Uyghur kitchen in Bloomsbury with hand-pulled lagmen noodles, polo and big-plate chicken; cosy family-friendly spot.

manchester.name: Purezza
manchester.note: Manchester's 100% plant-based Neapolitan pizzeria; every pizza can be made on a gluten-free sourdough base, and staff are well trained on allergens.

manchester.address: Hinterland Bar, 16-20 Turner Street, Manchester M4 1DZ
manchester.name: Wholesome Junkies
manchester.note: Vegan comfort-food spot under Hinterland Bar on Turner Street; known for its Korean tofu bites, truffle burgers and vegan mac n cheese.

manchester.name: Soots
manchester.note: 100% plant-based Italian bistro serving handmade vegan pasta (truffle ravioli is the standout) and sharing plates; the regularly changing menu can cater to a range of allergens.

manchester.name: Go Falafel
manchester.note: Long-running vegan falafel bar with several branches; build-your-own wraps, bowls and hummus, with daily rotating salads and fresh juices.

manchester.name: The Earth Café
manchester.note: Fully vegan Northern Quarter café; pick multiple dishes from the daily-changing menu plus fresh juices and smoothies, with famously good vegan chocolate cake.

manchester.name: Little Aladdin
manchester.note: Tiny vegan Indian café on High Street; affordable wraps including a vegan donner kebab, aubergine fritters and cabbage curry.

manchester.name: Bundobust
manchester.note: Award-winning vegetarian Indian street food paired with craft beer; reviewers praise its strong gluten-free and cross-contamination knowledge alongside plenty of vegan options.

manchester.address: 575 Barlow Moor Road, Chorlton-cum-Hardy, Manchester M21 8AE
manchester.name: Hungamaa Chorlton
manchester.note: Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice Indian street-food restaurant with an explicitly labelled menu covering vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and halal diets, plus a popular Sunday lunch buffet.

manchester.address: 9 Barlow Moor Road, Didsbury, Manchester M20 6TN
manchester.name: Levant: Elixir of Co-Existence
manchester.note: Didsbury sharing-plates restaurant with vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free dishes flagged on the menu; rated 9.7/10 on TheFork with a strong chef-led service.

manchester.name: Blue Eyed Panda
manchester.note: Cantonese restaurant praised for its vegetarian options and careful communication around coeliac needs; rated 9.4/10 on TheFork.

manchester.name: Sweet Mandarin
manchester.note: Coeliac-friendly Chinese kitchen with one of Manchester's biggest dedicated gluten-free menus (spring rolls, prawn toast, crispy beef); staff ask about allergies on arrival.

manchester.name: Honest Burgers
manchester.note: A coeliac must-visit: effectively the whole menu can be made gluten-free including burgers, onion rings, chicken wings and chips, with a dedicated GF menu.

manchester.address: 37 Hanging Ditch, The Corn Exchange, Manchester M4 3TR
manchester.name: Pho
manchester.note: Vietnamese chain at the Corn Exchange whose menu is 98% gluten-free and has been accredited by Coeliac UK for 9 years; staff are well trained on coeliac requirements.

manchester.name: Dishoom
manchester.note: Bombay-style Irani café in Manchester Hall with a dedicated gluten-free menu covering curries, grills, daal and cocktails; book ahead as it is very popular.

manchester.address: 5 Bury New Road, Prestwich, Manchester M25 9JZ
manchester.name: Ta'am
manchester.note: Kosher Middle Eastern grill and deli in the heart of Prestwich's kosher quarter; known for shawarma in fresh pita, pulled lamb and a standout lamb tagine.

manchester.name: Mozzarella
manchester.note: Kosher dairy Italian pizzeria with a wood-burning oven; margherita pizzas, creamy mushroom penne and falafel wraps make it a solid meat-free kosher pick.

manchester.address: 27 Bury New Road, Prestwich, Manchester M25 9JZ
manchester.name: JS On The Corner
manchester.note: Serving kosher food since 1965, this Prestwich institution does smoked pastrami beef, schnitzel and laffa wraps, with clearly vegetarian and vegan-friendly options.

manchester.name: MyLahore
manchester.note: Halal British-Asian fusion hotspot on the Curry Mile; butter chicken, lamb karahi and Sindhi biryani in a family-friendly, late-night setting.

manchester.name: Jafra Restaurant
manchester.note: Manchester's first Palestinian restaurant, a halal grill spot on the Curry Mile known for lamb makloubeh, musakhan, unlimited refill bread and a prayer room on site.

manchester.name: Ziya Asian Grill
manchester.note: Twice-awarded best Indian restaurant on the Curry Mile; the menu explicitly covers halal, veg and vegan, from pistachio chicken tikka to tandoori broccoli.

birmingham.name: Land Restaurant
birmingham.note: Birmingham's flagship fine-dining vegan restaurant, celebrating seasonal plant-based produce with creative tasting menus. A top pick for a special-occasion fully vegan meal.

birmingham.address: The Rainbow, 160 High Street, Digbeth, Birmingham B12 0LD
birmingham.name: BA-HA
birmingham.note: Fully plant-based kitchen inside The Rainbow pub serving vegan junk food done brilliantly: oyster-mushroom 'Kentucky' wings, burgers, Sunday roasts and brunch. The chef has a reputation for personally accommodating allergy needs.

birmingham.address: Unit B106, The Arcadian Centre, Hurst Street, Birmingham
birmingham.name: Cafe Soya
birmingham.note: Fusion vegan-friendly Asian cafe famous for in-house soy-based mock meats, satay tofu and mock crispy aromatic duck. Huge portions at very fair prices.

birmingham.name: Damascena
birmingham.note: Award-winning Syrian coffee house and deli that is fully halal, with a large clearly-marked vegan and vegetarian menu plus gluten-free options like hummus Damascena. Falafel wraps, fuul and flatbreads are standouts.

birmingham.name: Alterna
birmingham.note: Independent fully vegan cafe and bakery making everything from scratch, with oat milk as standard, specialty coffee and smoothies. Top-rated by Birmingham's vegan community.

birmingham.name: Zindiya
birmingham.note: Great-value authentic Indian street food with a dedicated vegan menu: bhel puri, veggie chaats, soya tikka bites and burgers. One of Moseley's best casual dietary-friendly picks.

birmingham.address: Orion Building, Navigation Street, Birmingham B5 4AX
birmingham.name: Tamatanga
birmingham.note: Bright, colourful Indian restaurant that is excellent with dietaries: separate dedicated vegan menu and gluten-free menu covering curries, biryanis and thalis.

birmingham.name: Milan Sweet Centre
birmingham.note: Pure vegetarian institution serving Sparkbrook for over 40 years: matter paneer, daal, masala dosa and Indian sweets at bargain prices. Informal, charming and reliably meat-free.

birmingham.name: Niya's Kitchen Pure Veg
birmingham.note: 100% vegetarian Indian street-food bar with chaat, tandoori and plenty of vegan-friendly dishes like pani puri and Szechuan noodles, in a cozy bar setting.

birmingham.address: 1355 Stratford Road, Hall Green, Birmingham B28 9HW
birmingham.name: Raja Monkey
birmingham.note: Lasan Group's vibrant Indian cafe-restaurant with strong vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options alongside its famous thalis. Stylish without the steep prices.

birmingham.name: Pieminister
birmingham.note: Pie specialist with a separate dedicated gluten-free menu including pies, fries and gluten-free beer and cider. A standout GF pick in the city centre.

birmingham.name: Chung Ying
birmingham.note: Long-established Cantonese restaurant in the China Quarter with a dedicated gluten-free menu (fried rice, sweet and sour chicken, wings) and staff praised by coeliacs for taking allergies seriously.

birmingham.name: Cherry Red's Cafe Bar
birmingham.note: Popular cafe bar where everything is clearly marked gluten-free and chefs take extra care when told a diner is coeliac. Reliable GF breakfasts, burgers and sandwiches.

birmingham.name: Pasture
birmingham.note: Upscale steakhouse with a dedicated gluten-free prep area and GF fryer, so coeliacs can safely enjoy steak, fries and desserts. The premium GF-friendly splurge option.

birmingham.name: Shababs Balti Restaurant
birmingham.note: Legendary Balti Triangle institution since 1987 serving halal baltis, with vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options (try the potato and pea balti). Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice 2026.

birmingham.name: Shahi Qila - Taste of Lahore
birmingham.note: Lively Ladypool Road Pakistani restaurant serving reliably halal Lahori karahi, biryani and mixed grills at moderate prices. Highly rated by locals.

birmingham.name: Mowgli
birmingham.note: Indian street-food chain whose meat is HFA halal-certified, with clearly marked vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free options throughout the menu. A safe, well-run halal choice in Moseley village.

birmingham.name: Central Deli
birmingham.note: The only dedicated kosher store in the West Midlands, inside Birmingham Central United Synagogue: kosher meats, poultry, dairy, bakery and prepared deli foods plus a vegetarian cafe. Note: Birmingham has no sit-down kosher restaurant; this is the verified kosher option.

birmingham.name: Wok2Vegan
birmingham.note: Fully vegan Asian restaurant doing katsu curry rice bowls, mapo tofu, satay mock-chicken skewers and chow mein. Top community-rated vegan spot in north Birmingham.

birmingham.name: Dishoom
birmingham.note: The beloved Bombay-style restaurant's Birmingham branch has a dedicated vegan menu alongside its famous black daal and gunpowder potatoes. Great for mixed groups with strong vegetarian and vegan coverage.

edinburgh.name: Novapizza Vegan Kitchen
edinburgh.note: 100% vegan Italian pizzeria, winner of Best Vegan Restaurant at the Scottish Food Awards; cosy family-run spot with gluten-free options across the menu.

edinburgh.name: Harmonium
edinburgh.note: All-vegan bar and kitchen known for creative plant-based comfort food like seitan surf n turf, plus a fully vegan wine list.

edinburgh.name: Soul Vegan
edinburgh.note: Plant-based Malaysian comfort food: aromatic laksa, satay tofu and banana fritters, with every dish on the menu vegan.

edinburgh.name: Holy Cow
edinburgh.note: 100% vegan café with inventive burgers, open sandwiches and cakes, plus gluten-free breakfast and brunch options in a cosy courtyard setting.

edinburgh.name: Seeds for the Soul
edinburgh.note: Health-conscious 100% vegan spot loved for nourishing breakfasts, bowls and gourmet desserts including its famous caramel cake.

edinburgh.name: Kalpna
edinburgh.note: Long-running vegan and vegetarian Indian restaurant serving authentic thalis and an all-you-can-eat lunch buffet since 1982.

edinburgh.name: Hendersons
edinburgh.note: Award-winning vegetarian institution serving since 1962, with inventive dishes like vegan haggis and lion's mane mushroom steak.

edinburgh.name: David Bann
edinburgh.note: Stylish vegetarian fine-dining restaurant in the Old Town with creative vegan dishes like smoked tofu and wild mushroom strudel.

edinburgh.name: Union of Genius
edinburgh.note: Edinburgh's original soup café with rotating vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free soups, chillies and salads at student-friendly prices.

edinburgh.name: Mother India's Cafe
edinburgh.note: Tapas-style Indian dining with a strong vegetarian menu and clearly marked vegan and gluten-free options near the Royal Mile.

edinburgh.address: Green Police Box, Lauriston Place, Edinburgh EH3 9AU
edinburgh.name: Tupiniquim
edinburgh.note: 100% gluten-free Brazilian crêperie in a historic police box; a safe coeliac-friendly spot with veggie crepes and sweet options.

edinburgh.name: Makars Mash Bar
edinburgh.note: Scotland's first mash bar: nearly the entire menu is gluten free, from bangers and mash to scotch eggs and sticky toffee pudding.

edinburgh.name: Mamma's American Pizza
edinburgh.note: Grassmarket pizza spot famous for Edinburgh's best gluten-free pizza, with GF crusts available across the menu.

edinburgh.name: Confelicity Bakery
edinburgh.note: Dedicated 100% gluten-free bakery and café by Chef James Chapman: naturally leavened sourdough, cakes, breakfast and lunch.

edinburgh.name: Alba Kosher - Chabad of Edinburgh
edinburgh.note: Edinburgh's only Chabad-supervised kosher food service: traditional Jewish meals made fresh in Edinburgh with 48-hour advance ordering (catering and delivery, not a sit-down restaurant).

edinburgh.name: Mosque Kitchen
edinburgh.note: Beloved halal Indian and Pakistani canteen by the Central Mosque; generous cheap curries with plenty of veggie and vegan dishes.

edinburgh.name: The Original Mosque Kitchen & Cafe
edinburgh.note: The original no-frills halal cafeteria at the mosque on Potterrow, guaranteed halal with vegetarian and vegan options on every menu.

edinburgh.name: The Clay Oven
edinburgh.note: Modern halal Indian and Bangladeshi restaurant serving fresh-cooked dishes with a wide menu for meat-eaters and vegetarians alike.

edinburgh.name: Lazeez Tandoori
edinburgh.note: Halal tandoori restaurant known for rich curries and kebabs, rated among Edinburgh's best halal picks.

edinburgh.address: St John's Church Terrace, 1 Lothian Road, Edinburgh
edinburgh.name: PULSE Plantbased HomeCooking
edinburgh.note: Small plant-based kitchen beneath St John's church serving rotating vegan home-cooked dishes with gluten-free options.

glasgow.name: Stereo
glasgow.note: Fully plant-based cafe-bar in a Mackintosh building with a creative global menu (banana blossom tacos, vegan fish & chips) and gluten-free options; doubles as a live music venue.

glasgow.address: 12 Kings Court, King Street, Glasgow G1 5RB
glasgow.name: Mono
glasgow.note: Pioneer of Glasgow's vegan scene since 2002; cafe-bar, record shop and music venue serving hearty vegan comfort food like mac-n-cheese and seitan burgers.

glasgow.name: The 78
glasgow.note: Cosy 100% vegan gastropub with a Mexican-leaning menu (birria tacos, cauliflower wings); dog-friendly with live DJs and a weekly pub quiz.

glasgow.name: Suissi Vegan Kitchen
glasgow.note: Family-run Malaysian vegan restaurant, often rated Glasgow's best vegan spot; handmade Asian-fusion dishes with no MSG and gluten-free options.

glasgow.name: Soul Food Kitchen
glasgow.note: 100% plant-based health-focused restaurant with wholesome bowls, raw cakes and cold-pressed juices; many gluten-free options clearly marked.

glasgow.name: The Hug and Pint
glasgow.note: Award-winning vegan bar and music venue with a pan-Asian plant-based menu (jackfruit curry, NYC-style pizza slices) and gluten-free options.

glasgow.name: Ranjit's Kitchen
glasgow.note: Entirely vegetarian family-run Punjabi restaurant and deli; fresh daily curries, thalis and pakora with plenty of vegan and gluten-free choices.

glasgow.name: Sylvan
glasgow.note: Vegetarian small-plates bar with a daily creative menu (baba ganoush, smoked tomatoes) and a rotating list of ~30 natural wines by the glass.

glasgow.name: Mother India
glasgow.note: Glasgow institution since 1990 serving authentic Indian home cooking; extensive vegetarian dishes (veggie thalis, aloo saag dosa) plus vegan and gluten-free options.

glasgow.name: Ubiquitous Chip
glasgow.note: Iconic Ashton Lane restaurant offering dedicated vegetarian and vegan tasting menus and a separate gluten-free menu; staff take allergies seriously.

glasgow.name: Cafe Swiss
glasgow.note: Cosy Byres Road brunch cafe famous for its gluten-free lunches, scones and cakes; staff are knowledgeable about coeliac needs.

glasgow.name: Bella Italia
glasgow.note: Extensive dedicated gluten-free menu covering pizzas and pastas, with dishes flagged on arrival; also has solid vegetarian and vegan options.

glasgow.name: Red Onion
glasgow.note: Modern Scottish restaurant with extensive gluten-free, vegan and vegetarian menus; reviewers consistently praise the gluten-free meals.

glasgow.name: The Brunch Club
glasgow.note: Brunch spot with a dedicated gluten-free menu (GF bread, eggs benedict, pancakes) and safety ratings from the coeliac community.

glasgow.name: Namak Mandi
glasgow.note: Peshawari restaurant serving 100% halal Afghan and Pakistani dishes (kabuli pilau, lamb charsi karahi); also runs a popular all-you-can-eat paratha buffet.

glasgow.name: Ambala
glasgow.note: Halal Pakistani restaurant since 1984; hand-ground spices, charcoal grills and handcrafted curries in a homestyle cafe setting.

glasgow.name: Eda Restaurant
glasgow.note: Halal Turkish grill house on High Street with mixed grills, iskender and pide; also offers vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options.

glasgow.name: Slamburger
glasgow.note: 100% halal smash-burger joint (halal since 2012) on Victoria Road; juicy burgers, loaded fries and sundaes in the heart of the Southside.

glasgow.name: Mark's Deli
glasgow.note: Glasgow's well-known kosher deli serving salt beef sandwiches, kosher haggis and gefilte fish; the go-to spot for kosher food in the city.

glasgow.name: L'Chaim's Kosher Restaurant
glasgow.note: Glasgow's longest-established kosher caterer and restaurant, run by the local Chabad community; classic Jewish dishes like kugel, brisket and chopped liver.
